key_idea: Let d_i be the row sum of player i. Summing d_i over a team counts its internal pairs twice plus the cross pairs once, so the cross terms cancel in the difference: S(A)-S(B) = (sum_{A} d_i - sum_{B} d_i)/2.
sketch: Compute row sums, sort them, and output (sum of the larger half minus sum of the smaller half)/2. O(n^2) to read the input, O(n log n) otherwise. Pitfalls: use 64-bit sums (row sums up to 1e9, totals up to 1e12) and fast input for 10^6 numbers; the result is always an even difference so the division is exact.
